title: "default object size" for <video> is not hooking into CSS correctly
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Following up from https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/7524 ...

In https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#the-video-element:default-object-size:
> The default object size is a width of 300 CSS pixels  and a height of 150 CSS pixels. [CSSIMAGES]

This sentence isn't quite right, as replaced elements (currently anyway) don't use the “default object size” in any way. (CSS itself does for e.g. backgrounds and list markers, in the [Default Sizing Algorithm](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-images-3/#default-sizing); but the sizing rules for replaced elements are much more complicated due to their min/max constraints, and are mostly still defined in CSS2.) However, the 300px/150px defaults _are_ defined for replaced elements in general [in the Sizing spec](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-sizing-3/#intrinsic-sizes).

So this sentence should probably just be dropped, and replaced with a note like:

```
Note: A video with no [=natural sizes=] behaves as if it had
a [=natural width=] of 300 [=CSS pixels=],
a [=natural height=] of 150 [=CSS pixels=],
and no [=natural aspect ratio=].
See [[css-sizing-3#intrinsic-sizes]].
```

Basically the only hook we really need here is the fact that there aren't any natural sizes. CSS will default the size appropriately.
